Tennish uses -ish with ten to express an approximate time.

Cannibalize is cannibal plus -ize; in its literal sense the verb denotes engaging in the activity associated with a cannibal.
Iceland is a calque of Old Norse ice plus land; the final combining form names a country or territory.
Screenland combines screen and -land for the world of cinema, extending the land element to a sphere of activity.
Leptogenesis refers to generating lepton asymmetry; its lepto- element refers to leptons and is historically derived from the particle name.
Lophotrichous refers to a tuft of flagella, with lopho- meaning tuft and trichous referring to hair.
Manifold contains mani- many plus -fold, from Old English manigfeald; it is unrelated to Latin mani- hand.
Mastectomy contains mast- breast plus -ectomy surgical removal and denotes excision of a breast.
Mastitis contains mast- mammary gland plus -itis inflammation and applies to inflammation of the udder in dairy animals.
Megohm contains the prevocalic form meg- plus ohm and denotes one million ohms.

Mesotartaric acid is the achiral meso isomer of tartaric acid, whose other stereoisomers include a chiral pair.
Mesoappendix joins meso- mesentery and appendix and names the mesentery supporting the appendix.
Myrioliter uses historical myrio- ten thousand plus liter for a capacity of 10,000 liters.
Cuban forms a demonym and adjective from Cuba with the reduced suffix -n following final a.
Silvern means made of silver and historically represents silver plus the adjectival suffix -en in a reduced -n form.

Hydropathy names the historical water-cure treatment, reflecting the extended -pathy sense of a treatment system.
Perihelion uses peri- near for the point in an orbit closest to the Sun, from helios sun.

Photojournalism uses photo- as a shortened form referring to photography, combined with journalism.
Physicotheology uses physico- for the natural world in a historical natural-theological approach.
Polyphobia uses poly- for polyamory and -phobia for aversion, referring to prejudice against polyamorous relationships.
Polyacetal uses poly- in polymer nomenclature to denote a polymer containing repeating acetal-related units.

Psephology uses pseph- in the extended sense of voting or election to denote the study of elections.
Coleoptile denotes a protective first leaf sheath; -ptile ultimately reflects Greek ptilon feather and has a botanical leaf use.
Purchase historically contains Anglo-French pur- forth or thoroughly plus chase, originally to seek or pursue.

Forwards illustrates adverbial -s appended to forward; the ending was extended from the Old English genitive to form adverbs.
Babs is a familiar form of Barbara with hypocoristic -s, a derivational nickname ending rather than an ordinary grammatical plural.
Selectron is the scalar spin-zero supersymmetric partner of the electron; s- names the scalar partner and electron supplies its counterpart.
Sesquitertian names the 4:3 ratio, one whole plus one third; sesqui- expresses a unit plus a fraction named by the following element.
